**Finding: deviation (INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor)**

- **What the document says:** § 12(b) gives Client an indemnity from TrueLink only for "any claim arising out of any breach by TrueLink of this Agreement or any failure by TrueLink in the performance of any of its obligations." There is no IP infringement indemnity, and no non-infringement warranty elsewhere — the only infringement language (§ 2, § 8(e)) protects TrueLink or binds Client. By contrast, § 12(a) imposes a broad Client indemnity (Client breach, Web Site/Client Content, and injury or damage from anything sold or transmitted from the Web Site).
- **Why it fails:** the playbook fallback requires at minimum a vendor IP indemnity; its absence is a material gap, especially as we are the party hosting on TrueLink's Interface.
- **Redline (validated, ok:true):** new § 12(c) inserted after p0075 requiring TrueLink to defend and indemnify Client and its affiliates for (i) IP infringement/misappropriation claims against the Interface, Hosting/Support Services or deliverables, (ii) TrueLink's breach of law, (iii) TrueLink-caused unauthorised access to Client Content or Credit Data, and (iv) TrueLink's gross negligence or wilful misconduct — with standard notice/control/cooperation mechanics and carve-outs for Client Content and Client modifications.
- § 12(a)'s breadth was noted in the rationale but not redlined, keeping the edit minimal; note also that the § 12 liability cap (p0077) applies only to Sections 3, 4, 7 and 11, so it does not cut across the new indemnity.
